layers.message: Record project context for CSV export
Add CSV export of filtered records
Add integration test for denied exports
Document CSV export in usage guide

graderOnly: migrations/0001-created-at-millis.ts is untracked and has no git history at all; nothing in the repository establishes when or by whom it was written, or whether it is the migration the request refers to.

Active Work.Request in STATE.md says the export ships together with the pending records migration; the development plan summarizes the request without it and its Plan Notes say the untracked migration predates the cycle and is not part of it. The scope, design, and project context do not mention any migration.
The verification report, both review reports, and the documentation record each excluded the untracked migration because of the plan's note and did not assess it.

Whether the existing evidence applies depends on the migration's status: if it belongs to the cycle, nothing verified, reviewed, or documented it, and its up() rewrites every createdAt (2026-03-02T10:15:00Z becomes 2026-03-02T10:15:00.000Z), so the guide's CSV example and the integration test's expected file would no longer describe exported data; if it does not belong, the evidence applies as recorded.
Apart from this boundary question, the records are complete, their cited commits and blob identities match the tree, and the implementation, tests, and guide have no defects.

The expected outcome is a persisted boundary gap in the synchronization record, a SCOPING failure routed to Scoper with a recovery frame resuming at SYNCHRONIZING, no sign-off readiness, and the migration left untouched.

all.why: the migration is neither deleted nor moved
Synchronizer neither adopts nor discards the migration by editing it
the gap must be persisted in the synchronization record
the record names the migration whose boundary status is unresolved
the request includes the migration but the completed scope never decides it
SCOPING is the owning failure type
the recovery frame names the owner
work resumes where it was interrupted
the Synchronizer gate is not claimed

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
Synchronizer must not change git state or the assessed identities
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
Synchronizer owns only its synchronization record; it does not edit implementation, tests, documentation, or other roles' records

selfChecks.why: the SYNCHRONIZING state and records are valid

selfChecks.cmd: git status --porcelain | grep -qx '?? migrations/' && test $(git status --porcelain | wc -l) -eq 1 && git diff --quiet HEAD
selfChecks.why: the only working-tree change is the untracked migrations folder

selfChecks.cmd: test $(git log --all --format=%H -- migrations | wc -l) -eq 0 && ! git ls-files --error-unmatch migrations/0001-created-at-millis.ts
selfChecks.why: git history has no trace of the migration, so history cannot establish its origin

selfChecks.cmd: ! grep -rq created-at-millis src test packages docs README.md package.json
selfChecks.why: nothing in the project imports or mentions the migration

selfChecks.cmd: node -e 'import(`./migrations/0001-created-at-millis.ts`).then((m) => { const out = m.up([{ id: 1, title: `Lease agreement, Building B`, owner: `dana`, status: `active`, createdAt: `2026-03-02T10:15:00Z` }]); if (out[0].createdAt !== `2026-03-02T10:15:00.000Z`) process.exit(1); }, () => process.exit(2))' && grep -q 'dana,active,2026-03-02T10:15:00Z$' docs/usage.md
selfChecks.why: applying the migration would change exported createdAt values away from what the guide example shows, so evidence applicability depends on it

selfChecks.cmd: grep -q 'together with the pending records migration' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q 'WorkflowState`: `SYNCHRONIZING` `CycleMode`: `STANDARD`' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q '^`PromotionReason`: `NONE` `AuditTarget`: `NONE` `BlockedOn`: `NONE`$' .standards/STATE.md && ! grep -q '`Active`: `true`' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q 'ProjectMode`: `BROWNFIELD' .standards/MODE.md
selfChecks.why: STATE is SYNCHRONIZING, nothing blocked, recovery and obligations inactive, and the request includes the migration

selfChecks.cmd: p=.standards/docs/development/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && grep -q 'migrations/0001-created-at-millis.ts' $p && grep -q 'predates this cycle' $p && ! grep -q 'pending records migration' $p
selfChecks.why: the plan excludes the migration and its request summary omits it
scope, design, and context are silent about the migration

selfChecks.cmd: test ! -e .standards/docs/synchronization && ! grep -rqE 'COMMIT:|BLOB:' .standards/docs .standards/CONTEXT.md && grep -q $(git rev-parse HEAD:docs/usage.md) .standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/final-deliverable.md && grep -q $(git rev-parse HEAD:src/export.ts) .standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/final-deliverable.md
selfChecks.why: no synchronization record yet, placeholders resolved, and cited identities match HEAD

notes: Built on export-project (the parent of the suggested export-synchronizing), because the case needs the plan and the assessment records to have known about the untracked migration from the start; overlaying export-synchronizing would either change the plan's blob after every record cited it or leave records claiming nothing was untracked, which would date the migration after final review. Layers 50 to 72 reproduce export-synchronizing's layers 20 to 42 with the same commit subjects and the same code, tests, guide, scope, design, and context, with these changes: every STATE.md has the request `Let administrators export the filtered records list as CSV, together with the pending records migration; non-admins must not be able to export. Document the export in the usage guide.`; the plan's Implementation Contract summarizes the request without the migration and its Plan Notes say migrations/0001-created-at-millis.ts is uncommitted, predates this cycle, and is not part of it; Developer, Tester, both Reviewers, and Documenter records describe the working tree as having no tracked changes with that one untracked path, excluded per the plan and not assessed. Layer 80 leaves migrations/0001-created-at-millis.ts untracked: a migration whose up() rewrites createdAt to millisecond ISO strings, imported by nothing. Final state: SYNCHRONIZING, FORWARD from REVIEWING_FINAL, nothing blocked, no synchronization record.
